project_name.description: Data Ventures supports New Zealand’s National Crisis Management Centre by supplying it with datasets and insights to support rapid decision-making.
project_name.title: Data Ventures COVID-19 Response Efforts
project_name.long_description: Data Ventures, a data broker and the commercial arm of New Zealand’s statistical agency, is supporting the work of New Zealand’s National Crisis Management Centre. This work includes supplying the centre with datasets and insights to support rapid decision-making as it seeks to limit the spread of COVID-19 in the country. It also includes the production of COVID-19 Population Reports, which seeks to measure the mobility of the population in six sectors: recreation; residential; retail; tourism; transit; and the workplace. These reports are created weekly and available for public consumption. The information provides residents an understanding of how the country is responding to the crisis.

project_name.title: Measuring Levels of Activity in a Changing City

thumbnail.filename_download: Measuring Levels of Activity in a Changing City.png
thumbnail.title: Measuring Levels Of Activity In A Changing City

project_name.long_description: Researchers with UDD, the University of Turin, University of Greenwich, and Telefónica Investigación y Desarrollo analyzed call detail records in Chile, focusing on the Region Metropolitana, to assess mobility as the country responded to COVID-19. Researchers found that patterns of movement changed as restrictions went into effect, spending more time in residential areas. Trips also became shorter and more localized.

project_name.description: The company Unacast launched a COVID-19 Social Distancing Scorecard to help organizations measure efforts to limit mobility.
project_name.title: COVID-19 Social Distancing Scoreboard
project_name.long_description: The company Unacast, which collects and analyzes location data to understand human activity, launched a COVID-19 Social Distancing Scorecard to help organizations measure and understand the efficacy of US public health initiatives to limit mobility. The resource uses aggregated mobility data collected from smart devices as a proxy for whether people are remaining home and analyzes it on a state and county level, assigning letter grades based on changes in movement compared to what is typical for that area. States and counties with large decreases in movement are considered to be successful in their interventions. The maps are searchable and updated daily. It cannot identify whether people are staying more than six feet apart.
project_name.participants: Unacast
project_name.short_description: The company Unacast launched a COVID-19 Social Distancing Scorecard to help organizations measure efforts to limit mobility.

By visiting apple.com/covid19/mobility, individuals can view mobility trends for major cities and 63 countries or regions. The data comes from requests for directions made on the Apple Maps platform. project_name.description: Habitatum and StateBook created a visualization of changes in population mobility in the United States.
project_name.title: Mobility Monitor
project_name.long_description: Habitatum, the data research organization, and StateBook, a business intelligence company, created a visualization of changes in population mobility in the United States. The site uses mobility data to estimate dwell time at specific locations and the daily average number of trips into an area (500x500 meters) that last between 15 minutes and 3 hours. Data is collected weekly and updates are published on a weekly basis. The researchers intend the resource to inform economic decision-making, help local businesses and governments understand demand for services, and help communities be more resilient.
project_name.participants: Habidatum International, Statebook International
project_name.short_description: Habitatum and StateBook created a visualization of changes in population mobility in the United States.

project_name.description: Enel X City Analytics and HERE Technologies created a mobility dashboard showing changes in movement across Italy.
project_name.title: Enel X City Analytics - Mobility Map
project_name.long_description: Enel X City Analytics, a company that provides technology and energy products, and HERE Technologies, a geographical data and mapping company, created a mobility dashboard for Italy, “City Analytics – Mobility Map.” Using anonymized and aggregated data from connected vehicles and navigation systems along with open data from open government agencies, the dashboard seeks to estimate changes in the public’s movements from 13 January onward. The information is intended to support decisionmaking by Italian national and local governing bodies as they seek to recover from the COVID-19 pandemic. The information will remain available until 31 May, after which the organizers will assess whether to extend use of the dashboard.
project_name.participants: Enel X City Analytics, HERE
project_name.short_description: Enel X City Analytics and HERE Technologies created a mobility dashboard showing changes in movement across Italy.

project_name.description: The European Union used telecom data to inform responses to COVID-19.
project_name.title: European Commission Joint Research Center’s Mapping Mobility Functional Areas (MFA) with Telecom Mobility Data
project_name.long_description: This report from the European Commission’s Joint Research Centre introduces the concept of Mobility Functional Areas, areas where a significant amount of intra-regional mobility takes place. The analysis is informed by data collected by telecommunications companies and is intended to inform policy responses to COVID-19, ensuring countries can institute mobility restrictions on specific geographic regions instead of nationwide.
project_name.contact_info: Stefano Maria Iacus, Joint Research Centre (stefano.iacus@ec.europa.eu)
project_name.participants: European Commission’s Joint Research Centre, A1 Telekom Austria Group, Altice Portugal, Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Proximus, TIM Telecom Italia, Telefonica, Telenor, Telia Company, and Vodafone
project_name.short_description: The European Union used telecom data to inform responses to COVID-19.

project_name.description: The news site FiveThirtyEight worked with a professor at Duke University Medical Center to analyze human mobility amid the COVID-19 pandemic.
project_name.title: Americans Didn’t Wait For Their Governors To Tell Them To Stay Home Because Of COVID-19
project_name.long_description: The news site FiveThirtyEight worked with a professor at Duke University Medical Center to analyze human mobility amid the COVID-19 pandemic. The analysis, which relied on mobility data provided by the location intelligence company Cuebiq, found that US residents did not wait for government orders to stay home but began reducing travel around 11 March. The analysis also found significant declines in social distancing regardless of a state’s political affiliation.
project_name.contact_info: Clare Malone and Kyle Bourassa, FiveThirtyEight
project_name.participants: FiveThirtyEight; Duke University Medical Center; Cuebiq
project_name.short_description: The news site FiveThirtyEight worked with a professor at Duke University Medical Center to analyze human mobility amid the COVID-19 pandemic.

project_name.description: Ghana Statistical Services and Fowminder want to use phone data to identify where mobility restrictions instituted are being adhered to on a district, regional, and national level.
project_name.title: Mobility Analysis to Support the Government of Ghana in Responding to the COVID-19 Outbreak
project_name.long_description: Ghana Statistical Services is working with Vodafone Ghana, the telecommunications company, and the Flowminder Foundation, the Stockholm-based nonprofit, are collaborating through their Data For Good partnership. project_name.long_description: The Dutch location-technology company TomTom releases an annual measure of worldwide traffic congestion using data from its navigation and mapping tools. project_name.description: This research study uses cell phone data to map the hourly movements of 98 million people to simulate the spread of COVID-19 in major cities.
project_name.title: Mobility network models of COVID-19 explain inequities and inform reopening
project_name.long_description: This research study uses cell phone data to map the hourly movements of 98 million people from neighborhoods to points of interests (such as restaurants or stores) and simulate the spread of COVID-19 in major metropolitan cities. The model is used to predict a variety of factors, including infection rates amongst disadvantaged socioeconomic and racial groups and key superspreader POIs. The study, ultimately, is intended to inform equitable policy response to COVID-19 across North America.
project_name.participants: Stanford University, Northwestern University, Cambridge University
project_name.short_description: This research study uses cell phone data to map the hourly movements of 98 million people to simulate the spread of COVID-19 in major cities.

project_name.description: University researchers used Cuebiq data to highlight changes in mobility before, during, and after movement restrictions were imposed in Canada.
project_name.title: Mobility and Proximity in Canada During the COVID-19 Pandemic

thumbnail.filename_download: Mobility and Proximity in Canada During the COVID-19 Pandemic.png
thumbnail.title: Mobility And Proximity In Canada During The Covid 19 Pandemic

project_name.long_description: Mobility Proximity in Canada During the COVID-19 Pandemic is a report from the Innovation Policy Lab at the University of Toronto to highlight changes in mobility before, during, and after movement restrictions were imposed in Canada. Using anonymized cell phone data, the report is intended to support decision-makers in policy and public sector to understand the impacts of social distancing measures on Canadian life. The report found that while movement levels have been largely restored, proximity levels have not increased and Canadians continue to avoid interacting with others.
project_name.participants: Cuebiq, University of Toronto
project_name.short_description: University researchers used Cuebiq data to highlight changes in mobility before, during, and after movement restrictions were imposed in Canada.

project_name.long_description: A World Bank research team used smartphone location data about Colombia, Mexico, and Indonesia, obtained from the mobility-data company Cuebiq, to assess the impact of pandemic-related mobility restrictions on real-world human movements. The research suggests that mobility restrictions contributed to declines in human mobility, particularly among those in the top decile of wealth. The piece suggests that further reducing disease spread requires allocating resources to respond to the needs of vulnerable socioeconomic groups.
project_name.participants: World Bank, Cuebiq
project_name.short_description: A World Bank research team used smartphone  data about Colombia, Mexico, and Indonesia to assess the impact of pandemic-related mobility restrictions on real-world human movements.

project_name.description: The COVID-19 Mobility Project is an effort to use telecom data to improve understanding of changes in mobility throughout the COVID-19 pandemic.
project_name.title: COVID-19 Mobility Project
project_name.long_description: The COVID-19 Mobility Project is an effort from the Robert Koch Institute and Humboldt University of Berlin to use telecom data from the Deutsche Telekom (distributed by the company Motionlogic) and Telefónica (analyzed and aggregated by the mobility data company Teralytics) to improve understanding of changes in mobility throughout the COVID-19 pandemic. The project maintains a "mobility monitor" which displays daily changes in the number of trips across Germany from March onward. It also produces  reports describing major findings following notable changes.
project_name.participants: Robert Koch institute, Humboldt University of Berlin, Deutsche Telekom, Motionlogic, Telefonica
project_name.short_description: The COVID-19 Mobility Project is an effort to use telecom data to improve understanding of changes in mobility throughout the COVID-19 pandemic.

project_name.description: The COVID-19 Mobility Network Modeling initiative seeks to model the effect of different non-pharmeceutical interventions on the geographic distribution of COVID-19 infections.
project_name.title: COVID-19 Mobility Network Monitoring
project_name.long_description: The COVID-19 Mobility Network Modeling initiative is a Stanford PhD student-led research project that seeks to model the effect of different non-pharmeceutical interventions on the geographic distribution of COVID-19 infections.  The project relies on data from SafeGraph, a company that tracks human mobility using cell phone data, collected between March and May 2020 across 10 large US metro areas. The resulting simulation demonstrates how infections occur hour-by-hour. An associated user tool shows to the reader how different restrictions, such as limits on restaurant services, religious organizations, grocery stores, and fitness centers, impacts COVID-19 cases over time.
project_name.participants: Safegraph, Stanford University; Cornell Tech, Northwestern University
project_name.short_description: The COVID-19 Mobility Network Modeling initiative seeks to model the effect of different non-pharmeceutical interventions on the geographic distribution of COVID-19 infections.

project_name.description: Geotab, a company that connects commercial vehicles to the internet and provides tools to analyze fleet actvity, manages a "COVID-19 Mobility Impact" dataset that provides users with information on changes in mobility due to the pandemic.
project_name.title: Geotab COVID-19 Mobility Impact
project_name.long_description: Geotab, an Ontario-based company that connects commercial vehicles to the internet and provides tools to analyze fleet actvity, manages a "COVID-19 Mobility Impact" dataset that provides users with information on changes in mobility due to the pandemic. The dataset describes congestion on highways and near airports and shipping ports as well as border wait time and port traffic using Geotab's existing fleet management tools and sensors. The company claims the dataset "supports critical decision-making for route planning/shift optimization," but there is little available information on current users.

project_name.description: CrisisReady was a collaboration between the disaster relief nonprofit Direct Relief and other researchers to investigate the value of mobility data for COVID-19 response.
project_name.title: Digital Mobility Data, Physical Distancing, and COVID-19 in Syracuse

thumbnail.filename_download: Digital Mobility Data, Physical Distancing, and COVID-19 in Syracuse.png
thumbnail.title: Digital Mobility Data, Physical Distancing, And Covid 19 In Syracuse

project_name.long_description: CrisisReady was a collaboration between the disaster relief nonprofit Direct Relief, researchers at the Harvard School of Public Health, Harvard Medical School, Stanford University, and other researchers to investigate the value of mobility data for COVID-19 response. Using data gleaned by Harvard researchers from the COVID-19 Mobility Data Network and Facebook (access to both obtained by Harvard) and data analysts based in Syracuse, New York, researchers created an interactive dashboard that could be used by the Mayor of Syracuse and others to understand changes in movement in response to social distancing measures, reopenings, holidays, and temperature changes. The project ran from March through June and intended to demonstrate how large, data sources could provide value to emergency response.
project_name.participants: Facebook, Direct Relief, Harvard School of Public Health, Harvard Medical School, Stanford University
project_name.short_description: CrisisReady was a collaboration between the disaster relief nonprofit Direct Relief and other researchers to investigate the value of mobility data for COVID-19 response.

project_name.long_description: Tectonix, a data visualization company, and X-Mode, a location-technology company, collaborated on an effort to measure social distancing, whether individuals were isolating themselves. project_name.description: The Zurich-based mobility data company Teralytics provides dashboards to health authorities, emergency responders, mobility providers, and transportation planners that can be used to better understand the impact of the COVID-19.
project_name.title: Teralytics Mobility & COVID-19
project_name.long_description: The Zurich-based mobility data company Teralytics provides dashboards to health authorities, emergency responders, mobility providers, and transportation planners that can be used to better understand the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on how people move through their communities. Johns Hopkins University uses Teralytics' dashboards to inform its risk assessments and decision-support tools. Germany's Robert Koch Institute uses Teralytics in its efforts to investigate disease spread and prevention. Italy's La Repubblica newspaper used Teralytics's dashboard to visualize the value of mobility restrictions and staying home.

project_name.description: TELUS is sharing insights with NSERC researchers free of charge and providing supervised and guided access to strongly de-identified and aggregated network mobility data
project_name.title: TELUS Data for Good
project_name.long_description: The Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council (NSERC), the largest funder of natural science and engineering research in Canada, and TELUS are working together to support government efforts to flatten the curve and reduce the spread of COVID-19. TELUS will share insights with NSERC researchers free of charge and provide supervised and guided access to strongly de-identified and aggregated network mobility data to be used by NSERC-eligible researchers that are studying and assessing the COVID-19 crisis. For research projects that qualify, NSERC will offer a $50,000 grant as part of their NSERC Alliance COVID-19 grants program.
project_name.participants: TELUS, Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council (NSERC)
project_name.short_description: TELUS is sharing insights with NSERC researchers free of charge and providing supervised and guided access to strongly de-identified and aggregated network mobility data

project_name.description: The #MOVID19 Hackathon was a competition hosted by the companies Numo and Datasketch, the City of Bogata, and several local civic organizations to develop innovative analyses of the COVID-19 pandemic and Bogota’s quarantine.
project_name.title: #MOVID19 Hackathon
project_name.long_description: The #MOVID19 Hackathon was a competition hosted by the companies Numo and Datasketch, the City of Bogata, and several local civic organizations to develop innovative analyses of the COVID-19 pandemic and Bogota’s quarantine. Participants used mobility data from the sponsor organizations hosted on Github. 44 people contributed, with three projects awarded small cash prizes. These projects included a digital tool to reroute transit and an effort to identify which clinics needed more mobility options.

project_name.description: Using data provided by the Chinese search engine Baidu, this project measures the effectiveness of non-pharmaceutical interventions in response to COVID-19 across China.
project_name.title: Effect of non-pharmaceutical interventions to contain COVID-19 in China
project_name.long_description: Using data provided by the Chinese search engine Baidu, this project measures the effectiveness of non-pharmaceutical interventions in response to COVID-19 across China. It analyzed first-party data capturing movement within and outside of cities, proximity and contact patterns, and the timeliness of disease reporting to construct daily travel networks and simulate likely outbreak scenarios. It then made these models, but not the underlying data, available to inform research and public decision-making.
project_name.participants: Baidu; University of Southampton; Fudan University; Virginia Tech; Wuhan Center for Disease Control and Prevention; University of Tennessee; Boston Children’s Hospital; Harvard Medical School; Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health; Sun Yat-sen University
project_name.short_description: Using data provided by the Chinese search engine Baidu, this project measures the effectiveness of non-pharmaceutical interventions in response to COVID-19 across China.

project_name.short_description: The Northeastern Mobs Lab COVID-19 Mobility uses Cuebiq data to understand how people's behaviors adapted in response to the pandemic.

project_name.description: Facebook has provided high-resolution satellite data to various researchers and humanitarian organizations.
project_name.title: Facebook Population Density Maps
project_name.long_description: Facebook’s high-resolution population density maps are designed to estimate “the number of people living within 30-meter grid tiles in nearly every country around the world.” These maps, available through the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX) data store, use a combination of machine vision AI, satellite imagery (aerial data), and census information to generate an understanding of population clusters across the globe. The maps have been used by a variety of stakeholders, from researchers to public health institutions, to support populations in need.
project_name.participants: Facebook
project_name.short_description: Facebook has provided high-resolution satellite data to various researchers and humanitarian organizations.
